historical_record.description: The Washington Grammar School, a twenty-room steel-and-brick school with an auditorium designed by the W. D. Shea Co., was built on this corner, the southwest corner of Washington and Mason Streets, by Condon, McGlynn Co.; it was nearing completion in June 1909.

The Recreation Commission engaged William G. Merchant, architect, to design a playground and building, to be known as the Chinese Recreation Center, on the former public school site in Assessor's Block 213 at the southwest corner of Washington and Mason Streets.

The Recreation Commission let the contract to demolish the old Washington School at the southwest corner of Washington and Mason Streets, the site of the Chinese Recreation Center, to Symon Bros. at $6,413.

The Recreation Commission awarded the contract to build the Chinese Recreation Center, at the southwest corner of Mason and Washington Streets, to H. L. Petersen Construction Company at $326,314, the lowest of four bids.
